summary: Belize combines ecosystem restoration, conservation and agricultural transition. Restoration pledges cover 5,000/6,250 ha of degraded grassland, 6,000/10,000 ha of forest and riparian reforestation, 8,000/15,000 ha of degraded-forest restoration, and 2,000/2,500 ha of mangroves. The grassland target equals about 20–25% of current mapped grassland, the forest measures 0.3–0.8% of current forest, and mangrove restoration 31–39% of mapped wetland. Conservation includes 6,000/8,000 ha of mangrove protection, 30% of Belize’s ocean in biodiversity zones by 2030, three marine protected areas proposed for IUCN Green List listing by 2027, and deforestation reductions of 0.05–0.6% in protected areas and 0.1–0.2% elsewhere. Agriculture seeks 15%/25% climate-smart and sustainable agriculture penetration and conversion of 4,500/6,500 ha of cropland to agrosilvopastoral systems. Cross-cutting goals are 75,000/90,000 ha under sustainable land management—area-equivalent to 29–35% of current agriculture—and AFOLU sequestration of 2,555/5,110 kTCO₂ e by 2030/2035.
